stemMd: Which statement must be true in every permitted order?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Chat must not be in position 4.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Alerts must not be in position 1.

explanationMd:
Combine the ordering and placement constraints rather than assuming one example is unique. The statement "Chat must not be in position 4." holds in all 6 permitted orders. Generate the cases by placing any fixed-position item and adjacent block first, then discard arrangements that violate a remaining rule. For each alternative, an explicit permitted counterexample appears in its feedback.

Complete permitted orders (each arrow advances one position):
- Alerts → Dashboard → Chat → Billing → Export
- Billing → Chat → Alerts → Dashboard → Export
- Billing → Export → Alerts → Dashboard → Chat
- Chat → Alerts → Dashboard → Billing → Export
- Chat → Billing → Alerts → Dashboard → Export
- Chat → Billing → Export → Alerts → Dashboard

distractorRationale.b: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Alerts → Dashboard → Chat → Billing → Export. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.c: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Alerts → Dashboard → Chat → Billing → Export. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.d: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Billing → Chat → Alerts → Dashboard → Export. Thus this statement is not necessary.

Rules Billing must precede Export. Alerts must be immediately followed by Dashboard. Chat and Export must not occupy consecutive positions. leave 6 valid orders: Alerts>Dashboard>Chat>Billing>Export; Billing>Chat>Alerts>Dashboard>Export; Billing>Export>Alerts>Dashboard>Chat; Chat>Alerts>Dashboard>Billing>Export; Chat>Billing>Alerts>Dashboard>Export; Chat>Billing>Export>Alerts>Dashboard. Choice true counts: a=5, b=1, c=6, d=1; necessary requires all matches.
